content.text:
I built the demo as a single self-contained file, `index.html`, with no dependencies. The script passes a syntax check, and I rendered it in headless Chromium and checked two screenshots. They show the platform, pillars, lintel, crown, crystals, portal core, rings, grid, stars, particles and HUD all drawing correctly. I didn't measure a real frame rate: the headless capture skips real-time frames, so the FPS counter read 0 there. Animation and the buttons were only checked by reading the code, not by clicking them.

**How it's built**
- **3D renderer:** written from scratch on the 2D canvas. It handles the camera, perspective, hidden faces, near-plane clipping for lines, and sorting everything back to front so nearer objects cover farther ones. Faces get simple lighting plus a rim highlight and glowing outlines.
- **Background:** a dark purple radial-gradient sky with two faint drifting nebula glows.
- **Structure:** a two-tier platform, twin pillars, lintel and crown cap, made from 6 boxes with 36 faces in total.
- **Crystals:** six octahedra (48 triangles) in cyan, magenta and violet. They orbit the portal, bob up and down, spin and tilt, and each has a soft halo.
- **Portal core:** a glowing disc tilted to match the 3D view, with four rotating spiral arms and an outer bloom. Two rings rotate in opposite directions, and each ring segment is sorted separately so the rings pass correctly in front of and behind the pillars.
- **Grid floor:** a cyber grid that fades with distance, pulses, and scrolls one set of lines.
- **Stars and particles:** 180 stars that twinkle and stay fixed in the sky as the camera turns. 110 particles rise from the portal and platform, sway, fade in and out, and respawn.
- **Camera:** orbits automatically with a slight up-and-down bob. You can also drag to rotate and use the mouse wheel to zoom.
- **HUD:** a frosted-glass panel with the "NEON PORTAL 3D" title and FPS / POLYS / PARTS readouts. Pause switches to Play, Orbit ON switches to Orbit OFF, and Reset puts time, camera, speed and particles back to the start. The speed slider runs from 0 to 3×.

**POLYS:** this shows how many faces are actually drawn each frame after hidden ones are skipped, which is about 40 in the screenshots. The full scene has 84 (36 box faces plus 48 crystal triangles). If you'd prefer the HUD to show the fixed 84, that's a one-line change.

After the first screenshot I made two small fixes: the "Orbit ON" label was wrapping onto two lines, and the particles were a bit too large.
